intro.text: Lindblad Expeditions Holdings, Inc. (NASDAQ: LIND; the “Company”) is a leader in global expedition travel, offering immersive, educational journeys that span all seven continents through its six pioneering brands. Driven by a passion for the planet and the belief that there is always more to be discovered, the Company leads travelers to the farthest reaches of the world with an expansive portfolio of ship- and land-based expeditions. In collaboration with National Geographic, Lindblad Expeditions operates and sells the National Geographic-Lindblad Expeditions co-brand, which offers ship-based voyages that allow guests to explore remote destinations alongside scientists and naturalists, and with state-of-the-art exploration tools.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.why: Securities held for the cash they will return: financial.

lines.name: Inventory
lines.why: Goods held for sale: operating.

lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Goodwill
lines.why: Paid for acquired businesses: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Deferred tax assets
lines.why: Taxes on operating income paid ahead: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current assets
lines.why: Other long-term operating items: operating.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Wages, services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Deferred revenue
lines.why: Customers' payments ahead of delivery: operating.

lines.name: Income taxes payable
lines.why: Taxes on operating income: operating.

lines.name: Current portion of long-term debt
lines.why: Borrowed money falling due within a year: financial.

lines.name: Long-term debt
lines.why: Bonds, notes and loans: financial.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities
lines.why: Other long-term operating obligations: operating.

lines.name: Other assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total assets minus the lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.why: Total liabilities minus the lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

s.t: Expedition sailing guests sourced from the U.S. represented approximately 90% of our total global expedition cruise guests’ ticket revenue in 2025, 93% in 2024 and 94% in 2023.
While Land Experiences segment guests from the U.S. represented 93%, 93% and 91% of Land Experiences guest ticket revenue for 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

The direct channel represented approximately 68% of expedition cruise guest ticket revenues for 2025, 75% for 2024 and 74% for 2023, which includes guest bookings through our National Geographic marketing partners and affinity groups and charters.
Land Experiences’ direct channel represented approximately 90%, 89% and 90% of Land Experiences guest ticket revenue for 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.

We also generate significant bookings from travel agents and wholesalers, representing approximately 32% of expedition sailing guest ticket revenue for 2025, 25% for 2024, and 26% for 2023, while Land Experiences bookings from travel agents and wholesalers represented approximately 10%, 11% and 10% of Land Experiences guest ticket revenue for 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
Fuel costs represented 3.1%, 4.1% and 4.9% of our tour revenues for the years ended December 31, 2025, 2024 and 2023, respectively.
Our competition within the expedition and cruise vacation industries depends on the destination and is fragmented.
We depend on shipyards to repair, maintain and revitalize our ships on a timely basis and to ensure they remain in good working order.

We rely on supply chain vendors and third-party service providers who are integral to the operations of our businesses that may be unable or unwilling to deliver on their commitments or may act in ways that could harm our business.
We rely on supply chain vendors to deliver key products to the operations of our businesses around the world.

Our ability to access additional funding as and when needed, including for new ship builds, our ability to timely refinance and/or replace our outstanding debt and credit facilities on acceptable terms or at all will depend upon numerous factors, many of which are beyond our control.
Most of our guests depend on scheduled commercial airline services to transport them to or from the ports or places where our expeditions start or end.
Because we rely on travel advisors to generate a substantial portion of the bookings for our ships, we must ensure that our commission rates and incentive structures remain competitive.
We rely on third-party providers of various services integral to the operation of our businesses.
Our ability to generate cash depends on many factors beyond our control, and we may not be able to generate cash required to service our debt.
Our ability to meet our other debt service obligations or refinance our debt depends on our future operating and financial performance and ability to generate cash.

Our ability to access additional funding as and when needed, our ability to timely refinance and/or replace outstanding debt and credit facilities on acceptable terms and our cost of funding will depend upon numerous factors including, but not limited to, the condition of the financial markets, our financial performance and credit ratings and the performance of our industry in general.
Accordingly, we will depend on the business of our subsidiaries to satisfy our debt obligations.

Accordingly, our ability to service our debt, depends on the results of operations of our subsidiaries and upon the ability of such subsidiaries to provide us with cash, whether in the form of dividends, loans or otherwise, to pay amounts due on our obligations.

Any determination to pay dividends in the future will be at the discretion of our Board and will depend upon our results of operations, financial condition, restrictions imposed by applicable law and our financing agreements and other factors that our Board of Directors deems relevant.
We generally rely on a combination of cash flows provided by operations and the issuance of debt or equity financings to fund obligations.
The valuation technique and inputs depend on the type of derivative and the nature of the underlying exposure.
The accounting for changes in value of the derivative depends on whether or not the transaction has been designated and qualifies for hedge accounting.
